script: There is a sea with no coastline. The Sargasso Sea sits in the middle of the Atlantic, bounded by ocean currents instead of land. It is named after sargassum, the floating seaweed that covers parts of it. Its water is famously clear and deep blue. American and European eels travel thousands of kilometers to breed there. Young sea turtles often shelter in its floating seaweed mats. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
